purpose: Codex is the only semantic model hub from product images to brand-film-spec. The repository supplies three-category profiles, reference evidence, schemas, deterministic gates, artifact naming, and a renderer port.

responsibilities: inspect one or more product images and keep per-image evidence
separate observed facts, inferences, unknowns, and forbidden inferences
resolve one of three primary categories and preserve extensible subcategory fields
generate genuinely different creative routes with explicit proof tags
score with the selected category profile and deterministic overall
decide whether a candidate deserves video-generation cost
write the final brand-film-spec and renderer handoff
optionally use imagegen for product-fidelity and continuity probes

model_policy.reason: Product truth, creative reasoning, evaluation, decision, and final writing must stay under one model context.
deterministic_code_controls: category profile validation and score weights

optional_plugins.use: Generate 3-5 still keyframe probes when product fidelity, human interaction, food physics, or cross-shot continuity is risky.
optional_plugins.boundary: Generated keyframes are review evidence only. They cannot replace source product images or grant new product claims.

subcategory_extension_contract.rule: Never force a misleading reserved subcategory. Use custom or unresolved and preserve a future profile candidate.

reference_policy: Reference samples calibrate proof order and pacing only.
Do not copy sample faces, packaging, logos, slogans, exact copy, product designs, or unsupported claims.
Do not assume the synthetic style of the samples is the desired brand-film aesthetic.

required.name: product_images
required.description: One or more product images supplied in the Codex thread or by local path/URL.

instructions: Assign a stable source_id and role to every image.
Keep product images separate from mood references.
Record conflicts across images; do not silently merge incompatible variants.
Populate product_identity, taxonomy, visual_facts, commercial_hypotheses, truth_boundaries, and dense_caption.
Cite source image ids in observations and taxonomy evidence.
Use visible material appearance when actual material composition is unknown.
Never infer clinical, health, ingredient, authenticity, material-purity, durability, or numerical claims from appearance alone.
Resolve exactly one supported primary category.
Use matched or provisional only when a reserved subcategory is defensible.
Use unresolved or custom plus subcategory_extension when the registry does not fit.
Apply legacy aliases only as migration, never expose them as current top-level choices.
User commercial inputs override hypotheses but never rewrite observed product facts.
Snapshot critical proof groups, scoring weights, claim boundaries, person policy, and renderer risks.
Do not default to avoiding people when the category requires application, consumption, wearing, scale, or carry proof.
Use exactly one of the three base templates as a pacing reference.
Subcategory differences come from category_profile, not duplicated templates.
A template cannot override product truth, claim boundaries, or critical proof groups.
Generate 4-6 meaningfully different routes, not wording variants.
Every route must declare product_first_seen_at, proof_sequence, required_proofs_covered, claims_used, and product_fidelity_lock.
Every shot must declare proof_tags and product_fidelity.
Cover every critical proof group before marking a route render-ready.
Reference pattern ids explain structure; they do not authorize copying sample content.
Score the v2 dimensions from 0 to 100 as integers.
Use the selected category profile weights; code computes overall.
Run structured category gates before render recommendation.
A high overall cannot override failed product timing, critical proof, unsupported-claim, fidelity, feasibility, or risk gates.
Eligible candidates sort before ineligible candidates.
Reject or revise recommendations are not render-eligible.
Profile score floors and category gate results are mandatory eligibility inputs.
Use when fidelity, people, hands, food physics, or continuity risk is material.
Keyframes must cover critical proof groups, not only attractive hero frames.
Reject or revise previews that drift from original product images.
Recommend at most one eligible candidate.
Return should_render=false when no route passes all hard gates.
State evidence, blocking gates, expected failures, retry budget, and candidate-replacement triggers.
Decision is about spending renderer cost, not about whether an idea sounds attractive.
Write the downstream creative-director specification, not a generic text-to-video prompt.
Include product truth lock, consumer proposition, category proof chain, time beats, claim boundaries, production controls, renderer fallback, and adapter boundary.
Do not invent brand history, brand name, slogan, certification, material, ingredient, efficacy, nutrition, authenticity, or numerical facts.
The package must be sufficient for a replaceable renderer without allowing the renderer to rewrite creative direction.
The adapter executes the accepted specification and returns telemetry.
The adapter must not rewrite product facts, taxonomy, claim boundaries, selected route, or proof sequence.
Retries and candidate replacement return to Codex.

adapter_contract: do not rewrite product facts, claims, taxonomy, selected route, or proof sequence
return adapter/model identity and output or job id
return failure telemetry and product-fidelity review
never silently spend a second render when retry_budget is exhausted
